claim: HASS.Agent's sensor configuration model gives each sensor a TYPE, an entity-name (must be entity_id-safe, no spaces), an update interval with a recommended default, an optional friendly name, and an availability-check toggle that decides whether HA treats the host as online before showing last state
stance_target: per-sensor cadence plus an explicit availability/last-state-retention policy is the incumbent UX contract — ha-linux-agent needs both an update-interval story and an explicit decision about how HA renders offline jupiterOS hosts
scope_conditions: HASS.Agent 2.2 docs (Windows); /latest URL redirects to the 2.2 versioned docs
quoted_support: TYPE: Select the type of sensor from the left ... Name: Enter the name for the entity in HA, this is the entity id so it must not contain spaces. Update Interval: Sets the interval for how often the sensor updates, the recommended value is usually fine. ... Availability check: Enable/Disable availability check, this tells HA whether to check if the computer is online before grabbing the last state.

claim: HASS.Agent sensors attach to the MQTT integration in HA under the computer's name, and the configured sensor Name becomes the entity_id
stance_target: host-name-keyed MQTT device identity (computer name as the device grouping) is the incumbent pattern for multi-PC fleets
quoted_support: Each sensor/command will be attached to the mqtt integration under the name of your computer. ... Note that the entity id is the "Name" you set in the sensor config.
